name: Vital Systems Corporation
old_description: Vital Systems was founded in 1986, the same year it was certified by the DOD to meet the highest standards in defense electronics manufacturing. Since then company has delivered defense electronics to the Navy, Air Force, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Raytheon. The experience gained in delivering crucial hardware for defense applications is the difference in the service Vital Systems offers its customers in defense and non defense areas.
about:
Vital Systems Corporation was founded in 1986 in Reno, Nevada, the same year it earned Department of Defense certification to manufacture electronics for military applications. The company has remained independently owned since its inception.

The shop specializes in printed circuit board assembly, box builds, and engineering support, with a focus on surface-mount technology that includes 01005 passives, BGA, QFN, and package-on-package placement. It runs both wave and nitrogen-assisted selective soldering, backed by automated optical inspection, X-ray inspection, and statistical process control.

Its customer base spans aerospace and defense primes — U.S. Navy, U.S. Air Force, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Raytheon — as well as industrial OEMs in the post-production studio equipment sector and automotive safety systems such as Tesla. The company also serves harsh-environment controls for energy and heavy machinery.

Vital Systems differentiates itself through an IPC-A-610 Class 3 mindset applied to every build, targeting 99 percent untested first-pass yield and 100 percent tested first-pass yield. It has offered RoHS-compliant soldering since 2004 and provides consigned and onsite inventory management with real-time MRP visibility. Customer relationships average 25 years, with one account dating back to 1988.

name: WCJ Pilgrim Wire LLC
old_description: WCJ Pilgrim was founded in 1998 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. William Jones, founder and current President, started the company with a focus on providing high-quality stitching wire to the Graphic Arts Industry. Over time, the company evolved to serve the Industrial, Baling, Brush, Packaging, and Automotive Industries. WCJ Pilgrim also prides itself on being able to offer solutions to many custom applications. In 2017 WCJ Pilgrim partnered with DDD Group and opened its first manufacturing facility in York, Pennsylvania. We are extremely proud to offer reliable, high-quality products that are made in America.
about:
WCJ Pilgrim Wire was founded in 1998 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, by William Jones, who remains the company’s president. Initially focused on supplying high‑quality stitching wire to the graphic arts industry, the business expanded over the years to serve industrial, baling, brush, packaging and automotive markets. In 2017 the company partnered with DDD Group and opened its first dedicated manufacturing facility in York, Pennsylvania, where it continues to produce wire products using domestic steel.

The company manufactures a broad range of wire products including coated and electro‑plated wire, industrial wire, spring and music wire, brush and broom staple wire, flat wire, stitching wire and custom wire solutions. Its capabilities cover custom base materials, plating types (copper, zinc, tin, nickel, polymer), tensile requirements, diameters and packaging. The York facility operates an eco‑friendly Electroshield™ electroplating line and provides wire handling equipment such as spooling and de‑spooling systems. A team of roughly 15 employees manages production, quality, sales and logistics.

WCJ Pilgrim serves customers in industrial manufacturing, graphic arts and publishing, waste disposal and recycling, medical device production, brush and broom manufacturing, HVAC ducting, food processing and transportation. The company also supplies baling wire for packaging and box‑binding applications and provides wire for automotive components.

The founder’s stated mission is to make the highest quality wire using the latest state‑of‑the‑art machines and components in America. WCJ Pilgrim emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 certification, expedited turnaround times, and the ability to develop custom wire products for niche or specialty applications.

name: Wald Wire & Manufacturing Co
old_description: We understand your need to have the most reliable and flexible supply chain partners so you can meet your customers’ demands. Additionally, you shouldn’t have to compromise on results, including delivery times, quantities and quality. Our 75 years of experience and our centralized Wisconsin-based location ensure you have the flexibility for fast turnarounds, short runs and immediate shipping.
about:
Wald Wire & Manufacturing Co. was founded in 1951 in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, as a small wire-forming shop serving small and midsize manufacturers in the Northeast Wisconsin region. The company remains headquartered in Oshkosh and has grown from a 9,000-square-foot facility with a handful of employees to a multi-shop operation.

Today the company operates over 200,000 square feet across three shops and employs more than 100 people. Its core capabilities include CNC 2D and 3D wire forming, spot welding, stamping, rolled and cut threads, in-house toolmaking, and tube and sheet metal fabrication with laser cutting, forming, and rolling. The wire-forming robotics produce items such as shelving, racks, baskets, fan guards, and pegboards in a wide range of metal materials.

Wald Wire serves both small-to-midsize manufacturers and Fortune 500 companies, offering no quantity minimums, fast turnarounds, and immediate shipping for short or long production runs. Customers rely on the shop for individual components, full assemblies, and end-to-end fulfillment.

The company emphasizes a “flexible, fully-integrated supply chain partner” model, promising “unbending results” through a relentless commitment to delivering quality welding, wire, tube, and sheet metal fabrication within the promised timeline.

name: Wallace Electronics Inc
old_description: Wallace Electronics is a Woman Owned Manufacturer of Custom Cable Assemblies and Electronic Enclosures. Located in Dallas, Texas, we have been providing our goods and services to the Electronics Industry since 1977.
about:
Founded in 1977 in Dallas, Texas, Wallace Electronics is a woman-owned manufacturer of custom cable assemblies and electronic enclosures. The company has served the electronics industry for over four decades from its facility on Miller Road.

The company designs and manufactures custom cable assemblies, wiring harnesses, and electronic enclosures. Its capabilities include custom fabrication, in-house overmolding, custom shielding and pinout design, reverse engineering from samples, and engineering support from prototype through scaled production. Wallace works with wire gauges from 30 AWG to 2/0 using materials such as PVC, silicone, and Teflon, and maintains over 300 applicators for precision terminations. The facility also provides continuity testing, pull tests, electrical validation, and environmental testing for vibration and temperature extremes.

Wallace serves a broad range of industries, including industrial automation, military, medical, automotive, aerospace, transportation (bus and rail), renewable energy (solar and wind), telecommunications, security, oil and gas, and food and beverage. Its customers are primarily OEMs and contract manufacturers that require custom cable solutions for specialized equipment and harsh environments.

The company emphasizes flexibility and partnership, offering connector-agnostic designs, design-for-manufacturability consulting, stocking programs, drop-shipping, and blanket orders to simplify supply chains. Quality is backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification, UL approval for wiring harnesses, and compliance with RoHS, REACH, DFARS/ITAR, and conflict minerals requirements. As a woman-owned business, Wallace highlights diversity and leadership in manufacturing.

old_description: Welcome to Warrenton Steel, your community's go-to destination for high-quality steel and metal products. We are dedicated to supporting your projects, big or small, with a vast inventory and the personalized service only a local steel provider can offer.
about:
Warrenton Steel is a veteran-owned steel supplier and fabricator based in Warrenton, Missouri. Founded in 1989, the company has served business partners across the region for over three decades.

The company stocks a broad range of carbon and structural steel products—including merchant bar, structural shapes, pipe, tube, plate, and metal building panels—and provides value-added services such as water jet cutting and mobile welding. Its inventory includes shims, flat bar, base plates, and welding practice coupons, supported by an extensive in-stock inventory and local pickup options.

Warrenton Steel serves construction, petrochemical, aerospace, power generation, and transportation industries. Its materials meet specifications for commercial buildings, petrochemical plants, aerospace components (AS 9100D certified), power plants, renewable energy infrastructure, bridges, and railways.

The company emphasizes its locally owned operation, knowledgeable team, competitive pricing, and commitment to exceptional customer service as key differentiators. Fast shipping and reliable deliveries are highlighted as critical to project success.

name: Washington Metal Fabricators
old_description: As more than just a typical "job shop," Washington Metal Fabricators is an engineering firm that specializes in optimizing manufacturing processes. While we don’t design products, we partner with our clients to refine their designs and determine the most cost-effective and efficient manufacturing strategies. We meticulously review every aspect of your product, ensuring it’s built with precision, delivered to market swiftly, and priced competitively.
about:
Washington Metal Fabricators operates from Washington, Missouri, about 50 miles southwest of St. Louis. The company was founded in 1979 and has served as a manufacturing cornerstone in the region for over four decades. Ownership structure and founder names are not disclosed in public materials.

The firm positions itself as an engineering-focused partner rather than a conventional job shop, specializing in optimizing manufacturing processes for clients. Its 154,000-square-foot campus includes a 50,000-square-foot assembly and distribution center. Equipment spans tube and sheet laser cutting (four Trumpf lasers, Trumpf 7000 tube laser), CNC punching, nine brake presses (38–175 tons), three coil-fed stamping lines, three rolling centers, 15 welding stations (manual and robotic, including a Genesis Versa2), 15 grinding stations, and a Nordson powder-coat line with custom finishes such as wood grain and corten. Services range from product consulting, 2D/3D CAD, and prototyping through fabrication, welding, finishing, assembly, and warehousing, supporting both prototype and high-volume runs.

The company serves customers from small local shops to Fortune 500 manufacturers across sectors including electrical enclosures, machine components, power-grid transformer tanks, OEM components, and HVAC products. It also collaborates with its sister company, EZ Fabricating, to incorporate non-metal materials and provide inventory management.

Washington Metal Fabricators was built on the principle that diverse equipment investment enables the most efficient manufacturing route for each part. By reviewing every aspect of a client’s design, the firm aims to deliver precision, speed to market, and competitive pricing without designing the product itself.

name: Wells Vehicle Electronics
old_description: Since 1986, Centerville has been home to Wells’s 200,000 sq. ft. distribution complex. This facility is equipped with cutting-edge packaging and shipping technologies, including proprietary packaging lines, automated order picking/stocking, real-time inventory control and a highly detailed product-management system with more 33,000 different item numbers.
about:
Wells Vehicle Electronics is headquartered in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin, with a 200,000-square-foot distribution and logistics center in Centerville, Iowa. The company was founded in 1903 by Robert Wells to supply electrical components to the nascent automobile industry, working alongside early innovators such as Henry Ford. The current Fond du Lac facility was constructed in 1983 and expanded in 1995, 1997, and 2013, while the Centerville complex has operated since 1986.

Wells designs, engineers, and manufactures a broad line of automotive electrical components, including ignition parts, emissions components, switches, sensors, regulators, solenoids, and relays. The Centerville distribution center runs proprietary packaging lines, automated order picking and stocking, and real-time inventory control across more than 33,000 active part numbers. The company also provides technical support staffed by certified technicians.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers, professional repair shops, warehouse distributors, and do-it-yourself customers across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. Wells has been a member of the Automotive Warehouse Distributors Association since 1947, reflecting its deep roots in the aftermarket supply chain.

Wells states its mission is to create innovative win-win solutions for associates and business partners in vehicle electronics, with a vision to be a dominant global solutions provider offering a broad selection of products and customer service. The company emphasizes sustainable practices, holding ISO 14001:2015 certification and earning the 2004 Iowa Recycling Award for Excellence at its Centerville facility.

about:
Widener Metals, Inc. operates from Fallsington, Pennsylvania, and has served Southeastern Pennsylvania and New Jersey since 2013. The business is locally owned, family-owned, and veteran-owned.

The company stocks a range of metals including structural steel, aluminum, stainless steel, and expanded metal in forms such as I-beams, tubing, and perforated sheet. It adds value through saw cutting, plasma cutting, shearing, punching, bending, priming, and painting services. The shop offers same-day or next-day service and will cut material while customers wait.

Customers span construction, manufacturing, transportation, and general industrial sectors, as well as walk-in retail buyers. The company notes projects ranging from large-scale construction to a middle-school science demonstration requiring a one-inch steel bar.

Widener Metals emphasizes its 35-plus years of industry experience, veteran-owned status, and a commitment to customer satisfaction. It differentiates itself with no minimum order charges, same-day or next-day fulfillment, and in-store pickup and delivery options.

old_description: As an expert for innovative molds, we have been fulfilling individual customer requests since 1949. The Wirthwein-Group employs more than 2,700 people in the market segments of Mobility, Rail Infrastructure, New Energy, Home Appliance, Medical and Interior Design. Wirthwein has always been a family-run business, which makes us independent and dynamic. We cultivate long-term relationships in the market. We are a reliable and stable partner.
about:
Wirthwein Fountain Inn, LLC operates in Fountain Inn, South Carolina. The facility was established in 2012 and operated as South Carolina Plastics, LLC until June 2020, when it became part of the Wirthwein Group, a family-owned business founded in 1949.

The site specializes in plastics technology, providing mold design and manufacturing, injection molding, assembly, and logistics services. It produces weight-reduced plastic solutions for narrow assembly spaces, complex geometries and surfaces, maximum-security components for rail fastening systems, dimensionally stable and temperature-resistant parts from advanced thermoplastics, and economic plastic components for white goods, stoves, and floor-care devices.

The company serves the mobility, rail infrastructure, new energy, home appliance, medical, and interior design industries. Customers include automotive manufacturers requiring IATF 16949 compliance, railway operators needing rail fastening components worldwide, and medical technology firms. The group’s global footprint spans 20 companies across Europe, Asia, and the United States.

Wirthwein emphasizes its family-owned independence as a source of dynamic decision-making and long-term customer partnerships. The group describes itself as a reliable, stable partner that cultivates lasting market relationships while delivering innovative mold solutions and global production strategies.

name: Yaskawa America — Drives & Motion Division
old_description: Yaskawa America's Drives & Motion Division produces medium-voltage switchgear (including padmounted gas-insulated switchgear) and low-voltage switchgear, as well as motor drives and controls. Designed for high-reliability power distribution in utilities, manufacturing, data center and commercial applications.
about:
Yaskawa America's Drives & Motion Division is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The division operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Yaskawa Electric Corporation of Japan, a company founded in 1915. The U.S. corporation was created to provide automation solutions and support to customers across North, Central, and South America.

The division manufactures medium‑voltage switchgear — including pad‑mounted gas‑insulated and gas rotary‑arc models — low‑voltage switchgear, variable frequency drives, motor controllers, electric motors, and robotics automation systems. It describes itself as the world’s largest manufacturer of AC inverter drives, servo and motion control, and robotics automation systems, and has produced quality products in North America for more than 40 years.

Products serve utilities, industrial manufacturing, data centers, and commercial buildings. They are sold through direct sales, partners, representatives, dealers, and distributors. The division also supports applications in packaging, processing, and general manufacturing, offering solutions such as data‑center cooling VFDs, the iC9200 machine controller, and the iQpump605 pump drive.

Yaskawa emphasizes a quality policy that places continual improvement and customer satisfaction at the forefront, stating it has set standards competitors strive to meet. The division’s founding purpose was to bring Japanese automation expertise to the Americas, backed by a parent company with over a century of experience in productivity‑improving automation.
